disease_label_per_paper: Amoebic liver abscess with large solitary right-lobe lesion and anchovy-paste aspirate
presentation_summary: 63-year-old Aboriginal fisherman presented with one week of fever and right hypochondriac pain, preceded by non-bloody diarrhea two days earlier.
Physical examination revealed hepatomegaly without jaundice or other signs of chronic liver disease.
CT abdomen showed a large non-enhancing hypodense lesion involving segments V, VI, VII, and VIII, measuring 12.5 x 9.8 x 13.8 cm, with internal septations and partial liquefaction.
Percutaneous ultrasound-guided catheter drainage produced odorless thick yellow-brown material described as anchovy paste.
Blood and aspiration cultures were negative, amoebiasis serology was positive, and the abscess resolved on repeat CT three months after intravenous metronidazole.
